title.text: Camiguin Sunken Cemetery & Guiob Church Ruins

title_en.text: Sunken Cemetery & Guiob Church Ruins, Camiguin

tagline.text: A village swallowed by a volcano, and a white cross over the sea

items.alt: A close view of the moss-covered coral stone wall of the Guiob Church ruins

children.text: A white cross watches over the old village cemetery that sank when Mount Vulcan erupted in 1871, and about 500 m away stand the Guiob Church ruins, where only coral stone walls remain. You can see the cross from the shore at no charge, or get closer by outrigger boat and snorkeling, in a half-day visit.

Out in the water off Bonbon, on Camiguin's west coast, a single white cross rises above the surface. An old village cemetery lies sunk beneath it, which is why the place is called the Sunken Cemetery. The gravestones remain under about
6m
of water, covered in coral, and the present cross is a concrete one that the provincial government put up in
. Before that, a wooden cross is said to have marked the spot.
The story goes back to
. Earthquakes began on the island on
February 16
of that year, and on
April 30
the ground split open about

southwest of the village of Catarman. A new volcano, Mount Vulcan, was born from that fissure, and lava kept pouring into the sea for several years. Part of the village subsided in the process and the cemetery vanished under the sea, while the residents moved to where the center of Catarman is today. There is a small irony in the fact that locals still call Mount Vulcan the "Old Volcano," when it is in fact the youngest volcano on the island.
The old village left one more thing besides the cemetery. About

from the Sunken Cemetery along the coastal road are the Guiob (also spelled Gui-ob) Church ruins. Coral stone walls of the church, traces of the convent and the bell tower stand without a roof, and a small chapel built inside the ruins still holds regular Mass. In
the National Museum declared both sites National Cultural Treasures. They are two of the three such sites in Camiguin, the third being the Spanish-era watchtower in Guinsiliban.

This is a place you visit for one view and a story rather than for spectacle. You can look at the cross from the shore without paying an entrance fee, ride a boat out to the base of the cross, or snorkel over the gravestones. It suits history lovers, sunset photographers, and anyone with a spare half day between White Island trips. The island's hot springs, waterfalls and sandbars are covered under
Camiguin
, so this guide stays with the two sites on the Bonbon coast.
You hire a small outrigger boat on the spot and go out to the cross. The fee is generally around

, but some operators say one boat carries 3 to 4 people while others charge per person, so confirm the basis before boarding. The base is ringed by a railing, which lets you see the cross from the closest point.
Coral-covered gravestones remain about
6m
below the surface. According to travel reviews, a snorkeling guide costs about
, gear rental about
, and a swimming fee about
. Visibility depends on the weather and the tide.
The coast faces west, so the sun sets behind the cross. The scene of the cross rising as a black silhouette under a red sky is the signature photo of the place. The boatmen usually leave around
5 p.m.
, so you need to arrive earlier if you want a boat ride.

A long, roofless nave stretches between coral stone walls. The thickness and height of the walls give a sense of how large the old church was, and a small new chapel stands to one side. The moss-covered texture of the stone is also good for photos.

blocks.title: Finding the convent and bell tower sites

children.text: Besides the nave, the sites of the convent and a low bell tower are scattered about. There are few signboards, so walk slowly and picture this as the center of old Catarman. A newly built white lighthouse can also be seen nearby.

blocks.title: The Old Volcano Way of the Cross

children.text: This walking trail climbs the flank of Mount Vulcan past statues of the 14 Stations of the Cross. An entrance fee of about
has been reported. The path honors the people killed in the eruptions of the 1950s, so pilgrims increase during Holy Week. Allow about an hour, depending on your fitness.

blocks.title: A look at Tangub Hot Spring

children.text: On the shore near the Sunken Cemetery lies Tangub Hot Spring, mostly submerged. Part of it shows at low tide, and you can also look at it underwater while snorkeling. Ask your guide about safe areas and the tide before getting in.

items.title: Half-day route (afternoon to sunset)
items.subtitle: Arrive before the boats leave and stay for the sunset

children.text: Leave your Mambajao lodging and head west along the coastal road to Bonbon. By motorbike or multicab it takes about
20–25 minutes
Stop first at the Guiob Church ruins and look around the coral stone walls, the chapel and the convent site for about
40 minutes–1 hour
. The shade makes it comfortable to walk in the daytime.
If you still have energy, climb a few stations at the start of the Old Volcano Way of the Cross. Skip it if time is short.
Move along the coastal road to the Sunken Cemetery (about
). Check the boat and snorkeling price list at the tourism center and pick your boatman.
Ride out to the cross or go snorkeling. Be out of the water before
5 p.m.
, when the boatmen leave.
Watch the sun go down from the rocks along the shore. The best time is when the glow spreads behind the cross.
Sunset comes at roughly
depending on the season. Because the boatmen leave earlier than sunset, finish the boat ride and snorkeling before dusk and watch the glow from the shore.

items.title: Half-day route (quiet morning)
items.subtitle: Get into the water while there are few visitors

children.text: Have breakfast at your lodging and head for Bonbon. The morning roads are quiet, so it takes a little over
20 minutes
At the Sunken Cemetery, take a boat out to the base of the cross and take photos. The sea is calmest in the morning when the wind is light.
Go around the area of the gravestones with a snorkeling guide. Take care not to step on the coral or touch the gravestones.
Move to the Guiob Church ruins to look around the walls and chapel. If a service is under way, pass through quietly.
Have lunch at a Catarman seaside restaurant, with grilled fish or seafood.
Finish the day by adding one nearby stop, either Sto. Niño Cold Spring or Tuasan Falls.
If you want to stretch the Catarman sights into a full day, you can add the waterfall and the cold spring in the afternoon, but this entry is planned as a half day.

From Manila, you can fly via Cebu to Camiguin Airport (CGM), or fly direct to Laguindingan Airport (CGY) in Cagayan de Oro and continue by land and sea. The direct Manila–Cagayan de Oro flight takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
. Seats on the Camiguin Airport routes are limited and sell out early in peak season, so check the carriers' latest schedules and fares.
From Camiguin Airport to the Guiob Church ruins is about
13km
by the circumferential road. The route runs through Mambajao town and then west, and you can use a motorbike, tricycle or multicab.
From Laguindingan Airport, take a shuttle to the Agora bus terminal in Cagayan de Oro, then board a bus to Balingoan. The ride to Balingoan takes about
2 hours
and costs about
The ferry from Balingoan port to Benoni port in Camiguin takes about
1 hour
. The one-way fare is about
, and sources differ, apparently depending on whether the terminal fee is included and on the operator. Ferries generally run from around
4 a.m.
to around
5 p.m.
, so it is safest to reach Balingoan by 3 p.m. at the latest.
There is also a roll-on/roll-off ferry between Jagna port in Bohol and Balbagon port in Camiguin, roughly once a day. Schedules and fares change often, so check the operator's latest announcements.

items.title: Getting to Bonbon on the island

children.text: From Benoni port to Mambajao takes about
30 minutes
by jeepney and costs about
. From Mambajao to the Sunken Cemetery in Bonbon is about
20–25 minutes
along the west coast road.
The most flexible option is renting a motorbike, about

a day with fuel extra. If finding your way is a worry, hire a tricycle or multicab with a driver and agree on the fare before you set off. In a map app, enter "Catarman Tourism Center" as the destination to reach the entrance of the Sunken Cemetery.

items.title: Getting to the Guiob Church ruins

children.text: From the Sunken Cemetery to the Guiob Church ruins is about
along the coastal road, a walk of a little over
10 minutes
. If you came by motorbike, it is easier to ride between the two. The ruins sit beside the circumferential road, so the entrance is not hard to find.
The Sunken Cemetery can be visited all year, but if you want a boat ride and snorkeling too, the calm sea of
March–June
is best. Rain is scarce and the skies are clear then, so sunset photos come out sharp. The base of the cross sits close to the water, so on days with high waves it is hard to approach.
From
November
to
February
the northeast monsoon brings frequent rain and high waves, and some days the boats cannot go out. Sunset then comes early, around
, so if there are no clouds you can settle into a spot in good time. In some years a late typhoon crosses northern Mindanao around
December
, so check the forecast.
During the Lanzones Festival, held in Mambajao on the third weekend of
October

, and during Holy Week, lodging across the island fills up quickly. In Holy Week the number of pilgrims on the Old Volcano Way of the Cross also rises. Some reports say part of the structure at the cemetery shows above the water at low tide, so asking locally about the hours when the water drops can add one more sight.

There are few large lodgings on the Bonbon coast, where the Sunken Cemetery and the Guiob Church ruins are. Most travelers therefore stay in the Agoho and Yumbing beach areas near Mambajao in the north of the island or near Benoni port, and make a round trip by vehicle. Simple guesthouses are said to cost about
for a double room per night and mid-range resorts about
, with higher rates in peak season. A small place on the west coast is convenient because you can walk out at sunset time.
Food centers on fresh fish and seafood. Many reviews say grilled fish, kinilaw and squid dishes at Catarman seaside restaurants cost about
a meal. Camiguin pastel is a popular souvenir, reported at around

a dozen. Souvenir stalls at the entrance sell items engraved with the cross and shell crafts, but there may be limits on buying and taking away coral and shell products, so it is better not to buy natural items.
Boatmen and guides usually leave around
5 p.m.
. If you want a boat ride or snorkeling, arrive no later than about
4 p.m.
. Watching the sunset from the shore is enough.
Check first whether the tourism center has a price list, and ask before boarding whether boat, swimming, guide and gear fees are per person or per boat.
Bring small bills of ₱20, ₱50 and ₱100. Boat fares, donation boxes and souvenirs are all cash.
The sunlight reflected off the water is strong. Sunglasses, a hat and a long-sleeved rash guard over your swimwear are handy.
For sunset photos, frame the cross and the setting sun together from the rocks on the shore. To reduce shake, use a tripod or brace your arms on a rock.
Mass is still held at the Guiob Church ruins. Keep quiet during services, and avoid short shorts or sleeveless tops out of courtesy.
Climb the Old Volcano Way of the Cross early in the morning or late in the afternoon to avoid the midday heat. You need non-slip sneakers and water.
The Sunken Cemetery and the Guiob Church ruins are National Cultural Treasures. Check the information center's latest notices and local rules, and follow them.
Mount Vulcan is a parasitic cone of Hibok-Hibok Volcano, and Hibok-Hibok is an active volcano that is still monitored. When checked on
October 3, 2026

, the alert level for Hibok-Hibok shown on the website of the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) was Level 0, but it can change at any time, so check the latest notices before leaving and while traveling.
This was a place where people were really buried. Do not touch or step on the gravestones, and do not touch the coral with hands or fins.
Currents can form around the cross depending on sea conditions. Always wear a life jacket and go in with a guide.
The coral stone walls of the Guiob Church ruins are old and crumble easily. Do not lean on them or climb them.
Boat and guide fees are often haggled over on the spot. Confirm the agreed amount and what it includes (round trip or not, time) first.
The road home after sunset has almost no street lights. If you ride a motorbike, leave before dark or use a hired vehicle.
It is about
20–25 minutes
along the west coast from Mambajao to Bonbon. For the whole island, with the White Island sandbar, hot springs and waterfalls, see this entry.
About
6km
northeast of Catarman, this waterfall is about
high. A road reaches right below the falls, so there is little walking.

blocks.title: Sto. Niño Cold Spring and the soda pool

children.text: A cold spring and a pool with a fizzy mineral taste, both in Catarman. They are good places to cool off after the sweat at the Sunken Cemetery.

In Guinsiliban in the south of the island stands a Spanish-era watchtower once used to watch for pirates. It was declared a National Cultural Treasure along with the Sunken Cemetery and the Guiob Church ruins, which makes it a good continuation of a history trip.
The gateway to Camiguin. It takes about
2 hours
by bus to Balingoan and then about
1 hour
by ferry. Adding a day before or after your trip makes it more relaxed.
